items.text: Soap and water remove many germs from the skin of your hands.
items.explanation: Soap lifts dirt and oils off the skin, and the water washes them away together with many microbes.

items.text: Bones give the body its shape and protect soft organs inside.
items.explanation: The human skeleton also stores minerals such as calcium and makes blood cells inside the bone marrow.

items.text: Red blood cells carry oxygen with a protein called hemoglobin, and an adult body makes about 2 million new ones every second.
items.explanation: Hemoglobin gives red blood cells their color and lets them carry oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.

items.text: The World Health Organization was founded on 7 April 1948, and World Health Day is observed every year on that date.
items.explanation: The World Health Organization is a United Nations agency. Its constitution came into force on 7 April 1948.

items.text: Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch helped prove in the 1800s that many diseases are caused by microorganisms, not by bad air.
items.explanation: Pasteur and Koch ran experiments in the 1800s that showed specific microbes cause specific diseases, which led to modern hygiene and vaccines.
